data.long_meaning: Derived from the Irish name 'Aodhagán', meaning 'little Hugh'. Named after St. Aidan of Ferns, a 7th-century Irish saint. The name Hogan carries the meaning “Little Hugh” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English. Parents who choose Hogan usually hope their child will grow to embody little hugh and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hogan total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Hogan" is of Irish origin and has been embraced by the Irish diaspora worldwide. Through its cultural dissemination beyond Ireland, the name "Hogan" has come to symbolize Irish heritage and pride. Notable Hogans in history include Michael Hogan, an Irish American writer, and Patrick Hogan, an American diplomat and politician of Irish descent.
data.spiritual_significance: "Hogan" is a name rooted in the Christian faith, derived from the name of St. Aidan of Ferns, who was an influential figure in Irish Christian history. Aidan is known as the "Apostle to the North" and brought Christianity to the north of Ireland. The name "Hogan" thus carries a spiritual significance of holding on to one's faith and passing it on to future generations.
